claims.quote: Whatever they may be, the council requires them to be settled every few years, and may require their settlement at any time if they are getting too large; for it is not intended that any nation shall run largely in debt to another, lest feelings unfavorable to amity should be engendered.
claims.description: An international council clears trade accounts between nations and makes them settle balances so that no nation builds up large debts to another.

claims.quote: To guard further against this, the international council inspects the commodities interchanged by the nations, to see that they are of perfect quality.
claims.description: The international council inspects all goods traded between nations for quality.

claims.quote: In national staples; a basis of agreement as to what staples shall be accepted, and in what proportions, for settlement of accounts, being a preliminary to trade relations.
claims.description: With money abolished, trade balances between nations are settled in agreed staple goods.

claims.quote: With every nation organized as a close industrial partnership, monopolizing all means of production in the country
claims.description: Every nation is run as a single industrial partnership that owns all the means of production.

claims.quote: How can a stranger travel in a country whose people do not receive money, and are themselves supplied with the means of life on a basis not extended to him?
claims.description: People no longer receive money; the nation supplies everyone's means of living.

claims.quote: It is arranged on a simple international arrangement of indemnities.
claims.description: A country receiving an emigrant pays the country of origin for the cost of raising and educating that person.

claims.quote: Subject to these regulations, the right of any man to emigrate at any time is unrestricted.
claims.description: Anyone may emigrate to another country at any time.

claims.quote: An American in Berlin takes his credit card to the local office of the international council, and receives in exchange for the whole or part of it a German credit card, the amount being charged against the United States in favor of Germany on the international account.
claims.description: Citizens pay with national credit cards instead of money, and travelers exchange them for a foreign country's card at an international office.

claims.quote: Not only is our cooking done at the public kitchens, as I told you last night, but the service and quality of the meals are much more satisfactory if taken at the dining-house.
claims.description: Cooking is done in public kitchens, and families usually eat their main meal at a communal neighborhood dining-house.

claims.quote: Every family in the ward has a room set apart in this great building for its permanent and exclusive use for a small annual rental.
claims.description: Each family in a district rents its own private dining room in a large public dining building.

claims.quote: If we expect to dine here, we put in our orders the night before, selecting anything in market, according to the daily reports in the papers.
claims.description: Diners order meals the night before from daily published lists of available food.

claims.quote: The mystery was explained when we found ourselves on the street, for a continuous waterproof covering had been let down so as to inclose the sidewalk and turn it into a well lighted and perfectly dry corridor, which was filled with a stream of ladies and gentlemen dressed for dinner.
claims.description: Retractable waterproof covers are lowered over city sidewalks in rain, turning them into lit, dry corridors.

claims.quote: The waiters are young men in the unclassified grade of the industrial army who are assignable to all sorts of miscellaneous occupations not requiring special skill.
claims.description: Young people serve in a national industrial army, and new recruits are assigned to unskilled jobs such as waiting tables.

claims.quote: Once more you must remember that there is recognized no sort of difference between the dignity of the different sorts of work required by the nation.
claims.description: All kinds of work are considered equally dignified.

claims.quote: The equal wealth and equal opportunities of culture which all persons now enjoy have simply made us all members of one class, which corresponds to the most fortunate class with you.
claims.description: Equal wealth and education for everyone have abolished social classes.

claims.quote: All the industrial and professional guilds have clubhouses as extensive as this, as well as country, mountain, and seaside houses for sport and rest in vacations.
claims.description: Every trade and professional guild has large clubhouses plus country, mountain and seaside vacation houses.

claims.quote: To save ourselves useless burdens, we have as little gear about us at home as is consistent with comfort, but the social side of our life is ornate and luxurious beyond anything the world ever knew before.
claims.description: Homes are kept simple while public and communal life is luxurious.

claims.quote: abolishing the market-place forever
claims.description: Work is no longer bought and sold for a price; the market has been abolished.

claims.quote: Probably humanity never before passed through a moral and material evolution, at once so vast in its scope and brief in its time of accomplishment, as that from the old order to the new in the early part of this century.
claims.description: Society changes rapidly and completely from the old economic order to the new one early in the 20th century.
claims.stated_time: in the early part of this century

claims.quote: There ensued an era of mechanical invention, scientific discovery, art, musical and literary productiveness to which no previous age of the world offers anything comparable.
claims.description: The new social order sets off an unmatched burst of invention, science and the arts.

claims.quote: It is bound to print all that is offered it, but prints it only on condition that the author defray the first cost out of his credit.
claims.description: A national printing office must publish any book submitted, without censorship, as long as the author pays the first printing cost from their credit.

claims.quote: The amount of this royalty is set to his credit and he is discharged from other service to the nation for so long a period as this credit at the rate of allowance for the support of citizens shall suffice to support him.
claims.description: Successful authors are released from their required national work for as long as their royalties would support them.

claims.quote: They vote upon the acceptance of statues and paintings for the public buildings, and their favorable verdict carries with it the artist's remission from other tasks to devote himself to his vocation.
claims.description: The public votes on which artworks go in public buildings, and approved artists are freed from other work.

claims.quote: The highest of all honors in the nation, higher than the presidency, which calls merely for good sense and devotion to duty, is the red ribbon awarded by the vote of the people to the great authors, artists, engineers, physicians, and inventors of the generation.
claims.description: The nation's highest honor, a red ribbon given by popular vote to leading authors, artists, engineers, doctors and inventors, ranks above the presidency.

claims.quote: Nowadays, when a citizen desires to make a serious impression upon the public mind as to any aspect of public affairs, he comes out with a book or pamphlet, published as other books are.
claims.description: Serious public debate takes place through books and pamphlets rather than newspapers.

claims.quote: The people who take the paper pay the expense of its publication, choose its editor, and remove him when unsatisfactory.
claims.description: Newspapers are paid for by their subscribers, who elect the editor and can remove him.

claims.quote: In the first place, the universally high level of education nowadays gives the popular verdict a conclusiveness on the real merit of literary work which in your day it was as far as possible from having.
claims.description: Everyone is highly educated, so the public's judgment of books can be trusted.

claims.quote: but the setting of his pathetic tales, the misery of the poor, the wrongs of power, the pitiless cruelty of the system of society, had passed away as utterly as Circe and the sirens, Charybdis and Cyclops.
claims.description: Poverty, abuse of power and the cruelty of the social system have disappeared entirely.

claims.quote: Till the war-drum throbbed no longer, and the battle-flags were furled.
claims.description: War comes to an end, in a quoted poem's vision of the future.

claims.quote: In the Parliament of man, the federation of the world.
claims.description: A world parliament unites all nations in a global federation, in a quoted poem's vision of the future.
